passage:
A fox was seen walking through a city neighborhood at night. Videos spread online, and many people were excited.
Wildlife experts warned residents not to feed it. Feeding could make the fox depend on humans or lose fear of roads and people.
Students studied why wild animals enter cities. They found reasons such as habitat loss, food waste, and quiet night streets.
The fox became more than a cute video. It became a sign that human spaces and animal spaces often overlap.
A city is not separate from nature. It is part of a larger environment, even when the wild arrives quietly under streetlights.
